repairs.before: First, the leader of the AI trade was hit by an outside narrative shock that had nothing to do with its latest quarter, and institutions de-risked in size on day one. Second, retail platforms reported record dip-buying while the professionals sold, betting that fundamentals would win — and they eventually did, but only after months of chop and a deeper drawdown before the stock reclaimed its high.
repairs.after: The mechanical parallel is an outside narrative shock challenging a richly priced AI leader. A dip-buyer starts with the most recent quarter and assumes the new threat will fade; a risk manager starts with the concentration of the position and asks what happens if it does not. Those different clocks can put fundamental conviction and near-term selling pressure on opposite sides of the same stock. A popular thesis does not set a floor when investors are reducing exposure, and a profitable business does not guarantee a prompt recovery in its multiple.
